CO2016B-P1-41.exp: Internal commands live inside the command interpreter (COMMAND.COM), which is loaded into RAM during booting and stays resident. External commands are separate .COM/.EXE files fetched from disk only when you actually type them.

CO2016B-P1-42.exp: Compaction (defragmentation) shuffles files into contiguous blocks and so removes fragmentation, but only until further creates and deletes reintroduce it - hence temporarily. It cannot always be prevented, so option A overstates the case.

CO2016B-P1-43.exp: The Power On Self Test is the stage where the BIOS checks the hardware and prints its version, manufacturer and date on screen. Bootstrapping is the subsequent step of pulling the OS loader off the boot device.

CO2016B-P1-44.exp: MS-DOS is a single-user, single-tasking OS - it runs one program at a time. Windows, Unix and Linux are all multitasking.

CO2016B-P1-45.exp: Invitation cards, greeting cards, brochures and posters are the textbook examples of desktop publishing work, because DTP gives the precise control over layout and graphics that such a page needs. A plain invitation can certainly be typed in a word processor, so option C is arguable - but DTP is the answer this style of question is built around.

CO2016B-P1-46.exp: F12 opens Save As in Word, while Shift+F12 (like Ctrl+S) performs a plain Save and Ctrl+F12 opens Open. The trap is choosing the ordinary Save dialog.

CO2016B-P1-47.exp: Portrait and Landscape are the two page orientations - the choice of whether the taller edge runs vertically or horizontally. Paper size is a separate setting (A4, Letter, Legal) on the same Page Setup dialog.

CO2016B-P1-48.exp: Word's Font dialog lists exactly four font styles - Regular, Italic, Bold and Bold Italic. Superscript is a font EFFECT, sitting in a different part of the same dialog, so it is the odd one out.

CO2016B-P1-49.exp: A mail merge needs three things: the main document, a data source, and merge fields placed in the document to pull values from that source. Word fields (IF, ASK, SKIPIF and similar) are optional refinements, not essentials.

CO2016B-P1-50.exp: The small squares on a selected object's bounding rectangle are sizing handles, dragged to resize the graphic. Move handles reposition rather than resize, and scroll boxes belong to scroll bars.

CO2016B-P1-51.exp: Word's Insert Table dialog accepts a minimum of one column and one row, so the smallest valid table is a single cell, 1 and 1. The question is worded loosely - it says document where it means table - but only the 1x1 answer matches what Word actually permits.

CO2016B-P1-52.exp: Word wrap is the feature that carries text to the next line automatically at the right margin. A carriage return or pressing Enter is a deliberate manual break, which is the classic confusion here.

CO2016B-P1-53.exp: The Thesaurus suggests synonyms, and in many entries antonyms, for a selected word. Grammar checking is a separate tool under Spelling and Grammar, so All of the above is wrong.

CO2016B-P1-54.exp: Double-clicking the right border of a column shrinks or expands it to fit its widest content - the same autofit gesture used in Excel. The left border belongs to the preceding column, so option A resizes the wrong one.

CO2016B-P1-55.exp: AutoCorrect was built to fix common typing and spelling mistakes on the fly, substituting the correct spelling as you type. Its later grammar and formatting tricks came afterwards, so misspelled words are the original purpose the question asks about.

CO2016B-P1-56.exp: Word Count reports pages, words, characters (with and without spaces), paragraphs and lines together in one dialog. Since lines, characters and paragraphs are all shown, the inclusive option is right.

CO2016B-P1-57.exp: Selecting the two seed cells and dragging the fill handle lets Excel infer the step and extend the series to 20. Edit > Fill > Down merely copies a value rather than incrementing it, and Paste Special cannot generate a series at all - so All of the above fails. The stem lost the figure showing the two starting cells, which makes it read oddly.

CO2016B-P1-58.exp: An Excel formula must begin with the equals sign so the cell is evaluated instead of stored as text. Typing + or - first also works because Excel silently inserts the =, a Lotus 1-2-3 holdover, but = is the defined formula prefix.

CO2016B-P1-59.exp: The colon is Excel's range operator, so the rectangular block from K2 to N12 is written K2:N12. A semicolon or comma would union separate references rather than define a range.

CO2016B-P1-60.exp: AutoComplete suggests a completion when the characters you type match an earlier TEXT entry in the same column. It deliberately ignores numbers and dates, which rules out option C, and its scope is the column, not the whole worksheet.
